title: Gender Differences in Orthostatic Vascular Stiffness Increases and Vascular Aging
content:
Early detection of signs of the vascular stiffness increasing in a young population may contribute to the development of more effective strategies for the primary prevention of arterial hypertension and other age-related cardiovascular diseases.
Aim of the study: To investigate gender differences in orthostatic increase in vascular stiffness during the head-up tilt test (HUTT) standardized by hydrostatic column height.
Materials and Methods: 133 healthy adults aged 18-20 years (93 females, 40 males) were examined. Blood pressure and pulse wave velocity at the brachial-ankle artery site (baPWV) were measured. An orthostatic increase in arterial stiffness was assessed during the passive orthostatic test (HUTT) using the Luanda protocol to standardize the height of the hydrostatic column. The functional reserve coefficient (FRC) of orthostatic circulatory regulation was proposed to assess the adaptive capacity: FRC = ΔbaPWV / baPWVb. This coefficient includes structural (baPWVb) and functional (ΔbaPWV = baPWVt - baPWVb) components affecting cardiovascular adaptation, which change multidirectionally with age. Results: Baseline values of baPWV (baPWVb) in the horizontal position did not differ significantly between groups and were within normal age ranges. However, baPWV values in the HUTT position (baPWVt) were significantly higher in men (p = 0.0007). In addition, dynamic biomarkers of vascular reserve, including ΔbaPWV and FRC, were also significantly higher in men (p = 0.0009 and p = 0.0064, respectively).
Conclusions: While baseline baPWVb values were comparable between genders, dynamic biomarkers of vascular reserve such as ΔbaPWV and FRC were significantly higher in men. Prospective studies are needed to establish optimal reference values for these dynamic biomarkers, to assess individual trends in vascular aging and the impact of treatment, lifestyle modification and other preventive measures on vascular health.
